# harness-review
A fortnightly self-review of your AI coding-agent sessions, packaged as a skill for Claude Code and
nightly self-review of your AI coding-agent sessions, packaged as a skill for Claude Code and Codex.
It summarizes your local session transcripts (tool calls, error rates, skills used and unused, subag
ent routing, hook activity, keyword-matched corrections) and has the agent turn the numbers into a s
hort report: what works, what needs attention, what is unused, and what happened to last time's reco
mmendations. The skill never edits your configuration: it is read-only except for the report it writ
es (and, with your approval, one memory note).
## Privacy
- The script reads transcript files on your machine (`~/.claude/projects` or `~/.codex/sessions`) an

d prints a Markdown summary. It makes no network requests and sends nothing anywhere.
- The report h
olds counts, tool names, skill names, project directory names and short error messages (digits norma
lized, truncated to 100 characters). Before printing, error texts and snippets are redacted on a bes
t-effort basis: your home directory and other `/Users/<name>` or `/home/<name>` paths become `~`, an
d credential-looking strings (`key=value` pairs, bearer tokens, common API-key prefixes, JWTs, URL p
asswords, long random tokens) and file contents quoted in edit errors are removed. Redaction is heur

istic, so read the report before sharing it.
- User messages are not quoted unless you pass `--inclu
de-corrections`, which adds redacted snippets of at most 160 characters. Which messages count as cor
rections is a keyword match (Russian and English phrases such as "that's wrong" or "undo"); treat th

e number as a hint, not a measurement.
- The skill itself runs inside your agent, so the report is r
ead by the model you already use. Check it before sharing.

DeepSeek Harness (package `plugins/dsh-harness-review`, a skill provider with a `cordis.patch.yml` b
rness (package `plugins/dsh-harness-review`, a skill provider with a `cordis.patch.yml` bundle row):
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The skill defaults to Claude Code transcripts (`--agent claude`) and can review Codex sessions with
`--agent codex`; DeepSeek Harness's own transcripts are not supported.
Then ask: "review my agent sessions" or "run a harness health check".
## Running every two weeks
Ask the agent manually, or schedule it from the agent itself: a Claude Code `/schedule` routine, or
a scheduled task in the Claude or Codex desktop app, with the prompt "Run the harness-review skill".
A plain cron job that launches `claude` or `codex` is not recommended: it runs unattended with your
permissions and without a place to show the result.
## Reports
The skill looks for the previous review and saves the new one in this order:

1. A Drafta note titled `AUDIT — harness — <date>`, when a `drafta` MCP server is connected.
2. Othe
rwise `harness-review-<date>.md` in `~/.local/share/harness-review/`.
If a memory MCP server is configured, a cross-project lesson found during the review may be saved th
memory MCP server is configured, a cross-project lesson found during the review may be saved there.
## Script
`plugins/harness-review/scripts/session-audit` is a Python 3 script using only the standard library.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
- `--agent` selects the transcript format. Claude Code reads `~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl`; Codex

reads `~/.codex/sessions/**/rollout-*.jsonl`.
- The window is applied to each record's timestamp, no

t the file's modification time. Default: last 14 days.
- `--split` adds before/after columns for sub

agent routing and main-thread code edits, to measure a rule change.
- `--skills-dir` defaults to `~/
.claude/skills` or `~/.codex/skills`; installed skills never called in the window are listed as unus
ed. Installed means user skills plus plugin skills found in a `plugins` directory beside it; project

-level skills are not discovered. Slash-command use (`<command-name>`) counts as use.
- Unreadable o
r vanished transcript files are skipped and counted in the report; malformed lines are counted too.
- `--hooks` counts the given hook names in tool results; `--memory-tool` enables a "memory search be
fore first code read" section; `--metrics-file` adds a TSV of external executor runs (columns `time`

in UTC, `model`, `subtype`). Each section is omitted when its option is not given.
- Codex transcri
pts have no interrupt, compaction or model-override records; the report lists these as not available
ts have no interrupt, compaction or model-override records; the report lists these as not available.
## Development
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The Claude Code plugin under `plugins/harness-review` holds the canonical script and skill. `plugins
/harness-review-codex` and `plugins/dsh-harness-review` carry a copy of the script and a skill deriv
ed from it, because those packages must be self-contained. The DeepSeek Harness package has its own
check: `npm test` in that directory.

## Test scope

- Task checks: `TEST_BASE=<base> python3 scripts/test-policy.py <component>`.
- Preview selection: a

dd `--plan`; see `.test-policy.json` for component names.
- Release verification: `TEST_MODE=release

python3 scripts/test-policy.py all`.
- Immediate manual testing: `TEST_MODE=manual` plus the usual

build/package
command. Tests are not run; the artifact is not a verified release.

CI defaults to targeted tests; select `test_mode=release` or `manual` when
dispatching a workflow th

at offers these inputs. A source/dependency change can
affect several components. Full browser/app-h

osted suites require release mode;
run explicit scenario tests separately for task acceptance. Exist

ing deployment
permissions and data guards still apply.
